parts.name: bible (fill the whole Book Bible)
parts.about: Only when the run setting “Fill the whole Book Bible” (`fill_bible`) is on: after the chapter outline and before chapter one, every empty field of every Book Bible page is filled in batched AI calls (18 calls for the Practice AI's short story, two rounds) and approved under the run's consent. It must never replace the author's own text and never hold up the book. *Not tested here:* the 🤖 side-by-side fill through Claude Code helpers (`claude_code_speed.BibleHelper`; the harness switches Claude Code off) and the 📖 button's own job beyond D-11-s.

results.title: the AI times out (once; and every time)
results.happened: Once: The book finished with nothing lost. — Every time: The book finished with nothing lost. — Every time (counted): The book finished with nothing lost. Bible step: “0 sections filled, 40 still empty (40: the AI did not answer for it)”; 30 bible call(s), 30 faulted; 30 BIBLE_FILL_LATER note(s).
risks: every call timed out and the step still asked all 30 batches one after another (both rounds; no “give up after a few time-outs”): with AutoInjector's real 240 s time limit that is about 120 minutes of waiting in an optional step before chapter one
30 identical “could not be filled now (TIMEOUT)” warnings flood the run journal

finding.where: akowe/akowe/whole_bible.py `fill` (lines ~440-476) and `run_step` (lines ~515-563) (the loop over every batch, both rounds, with no early stop)
finding.cause: A failed batch is noted and the loop goes on to the next batch, then round 2 asks the failed ones once more; nothing stops after a run of time-outs. With a real web AI each time-out costs the full provider time limit (AutoInjector 240 s), and each failure writes its own warning line.
finding.fix: After 2–3 consecutive time-outs / unavailable answers, stop the step with one note (“the AI is not answering — the rest is decided just in time; 📖 Fill in the whole Book Bible later”).
finding.what: When the AI keeps timing out the optional step still waits out every batch (about 2 hours with the real 240 s limit) and floods the journal with identical warnings

results.title: every AI at its usage limit, then recovers
results.happened: Every AI at its usage limit for 6 calls, then free: The book finished with nothing lost. Bible step: “46 sections filled, 3 still empty (2: the AI did not answer for it; 1: the AI had nothing to add yet)”; 24 bible call(s), 6 faulted; 1 BIBLE_FILL_LATER note(s). — Usage limit for the whole step: The book finished with nothing lost. Bible step: “0 sections filled, 40 still empty (40: the AI did not answer for it)”; 180 bible call(s), 180 faulted; 30 BIBLE_FILL_LATER note(s).
risks: at a usage limit the step does not wait (every other step does): it gives up every batch at once (180 calls) and the author's “fill everything” ends with “0 sections filled, 40 still empty (40: the AI did not answer for it)”; the notes show the code UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE and “the AI did not answer for it”, never “usage limit — try 📖 Fill in the whole Book Bible later”

finding.cause: A usage-limited answer is an ordinary AkoweError for `fill`, so each batch fails at once and the step ends without the usage-limit wait every other step does; the note says “could not be filled now (UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE)” and the summary “the AI did not answer for it”.
finding.fix: Name the usage limit in the note (and when it resets), and point to 📖 Fill in the whole Book Bible for later; or wait for the limit like the other steps when the author asked for the whole Bible.
finding.what: At a usage limit the whole-Bible fill gives up instead of waiting and the note does not say “usage limit”

finding.where: akowe/akowe/whole_bible.py `fill` (lines ~440-476) and `run_step` (lines ~515-563); the stop itself is akowe/akowe/autobook.py `_run` (line ~1510, INTERNAL_ERROR)
finding.cause: `fill` catches only `AkoweError` per batch (an AI error); any other exception (a bug in `accept`, an OSError when the dossier is written, a KeyError in a store) is re-raised after the summary, and `run_step` re-raises it too, so the run's generic handler pauses the whole book with INTERNAL_ERROR. The alert then files it under “AI problem” (as A-2-g).
finding.fix: In `run_step`, catch `Exception` (not the run's pause / cancel controls) around `fill`, log it once, add a coded note (BIBLE_FILL_LATER / BIBLE_FILL_FAILED) and let the book go on, as the step's own text promises.
finding.what: An unexpected error inside the optional Book Bible fill stops the whole book (INTERNAL_ERROR, filed as an AI problem); ▶ Resume finishes it

results.title: the most likely real-life problem: a web AI answers a 36-field batch but leaves out a couple of fields (and wraps the JSON in a ```json fence)
results.happened: Two fields missing from every answer: The book finished with nothing lost. Bible step: “0 sections filled, 40 still empty (40: the AI did not answer for it)”; 90 bible call(s), 90 faulted; 30 BIBLE_FILL_LATER note(s).
risks: every batch was thrown away because 2 of its fields were missing: 0 sections filled after 90 calls (each batch asked 3 times, only on AI-1); the step says “0 sections filled, 40 still empty (40: the AI did not answer for it)” although the AI DID answer the other fields

finding.where: akowe/akowe/whole_bible.py `schema` (line ~278: every asked key is `required`, `additionalProperties: false`) against `read_answer` (line ~284, which already tolerates missing and empty keys); the re-asks are in the adapter (providers.py) via assist `_call_ai`
finding.cause: The schema makes every one of up to 36 keys required, so an answer that leaves out one or two is refused by the adapter's schema check and re-asked (3 times) on the same AI; then the whole batch is dropped as “the AI did not answer for it”. Web AIs routinely skip a field or two in a 36-field object, so the tolerant `read_answer` never gets to run.
finding.fix: Send the schema with `required: []` (or only the keys of the first subject) and let `read_answer` take what came; say “the AI left N field(s) empty” instead of “did not answer”.
finding.what: One or two missing fields per answer and the whole Book Bible fill is thrown away (0 sections filled, ~3× the calls), reported as “the AI did not answer”

results.title: a batch answer fills the WRONG page: (1) the values of subject 1 and 2 swapped (valid keys); (2) keys of subjects that are not in this batch
results.happened: (1) Answers for subjects 1 and 2 swapped: The book finished with nothing lost. — (2) Keys of subject s9 (not in the batch) instead of s1, 4 times: The book finished with nothing lost. Bible step: “41 sections filled, 7 still empty (3: the AI did not answer for it; 4: the AI had nothing to add yet)”; 22 bible call(s), 4 faulted; 1 BIBLE_FILL_LATER note(s).
risks: 17 field(s) on one page now describe ANOTHER subject (the batch's answers for subject 1 and 2 were swapped) and were approved at once under the run's consent; nothing checks that an answer names its own subject

finding.cause: Answers are matched only by key (`s1__…`); a batch packs several subjects, and an AI that mixes up two rows writes one subject's description into the other's page. `accept` approves it at once under the run's consent (`by=run:<id>`), and later chapters must match it (🔒 once used).
finding.fix: Cheap check before accepting: a value that names another subject of the same batch (and not its own) is kept as a proposal (not approved) or dropped and re-asked alone.
finding.what: A mixed-up batch answer puts one character's / place's details on another's page and approves them

results.title: a huge Book Bible: 120 extra places and 60 extra items before the step, and every answer field a 2 MB string
results.happened: 180 extra records + 2 MB answers: The book finished with nothing lost. Bible step: “1485 sections filled, 2 still empty (2: the AI had nothing to add yet)”; 561 bible call(s), 3 faulted; 0 BIBLE_FILL_LATER note(s). 561 bible calls; longest stored field 600 characters; 142 s in all.
risks: 561 AI calls for one optional step

finding.cause: Every record with any open field costs at least one share of a call, and every record type has many fields (a place dossier ~30); 180 extra records needed 561 calls. Nothing caps the step or warns before it starts; with a web AI at ~30-60 s per call this is many hours before chapter one. (The 2 MB answers were clipped to 600 characters: fine.)
finding.fix: Before the step, show the number of calls it will make (and a time estimate) and cap it (e.g. the main records first, the rest left for just in time / 📖 later).
finding.what: A big Book Bible makes the optional step hundreds of AI calls long (561 for 180 extra records)

finding.where: akowe/akowe/whole_bible.py `fill` (line ~459-462: `accept` is outside the per-batch `except AkoweError`) -> akowe/akowe/forge_kinds.py `apply_proposals` / `mutate` (raises NOT_FOUND for a deleted dossier); stop in autobook.py `_run` `except AkoweError` (line ~1495)
finding.cause: Only the AI call (`ask`) is inside the per-batch try; when the author deletes a place (or item / magic) while its batch is out, `accept` raises NOT_FOUND, `fill` re-raises it and the run pauses as for an AI error. The author's typed text in another field was kept (the empty-field check happens when the answer is applied).
finding.fix: Put `accept` (per part) inside the per-batch try in `fill`: a record that is gone is skipped with a note; a run never pauses for it.
finding.what: Deleting a place while the optional Book Bible fill runs pauses the whole book with NOT_FOUND
